subject: CheckoutFlow live: sudden throughput collapse tied to client header merge bug
messages:
From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@checkoutflow.io>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: eng@checkoutflow.io, support@checkoutflow.io
Date: 2027-03-25T16:12:00Z
Subject: Live ingestion incident — p99 latency spike and error-rate surge

Hi Markus,

We just started seeing a major throughput collapse on our production CheckoutFlow integration around 15:50 UTC. P95 is fine but p99 shot up to ~18s and the edge shows repeated 502/504 errors. This started immediately after a deploy of CheckoutFlow client 2.4.1 (your SDK).

Live metrics:
- Traffic: ~1.2k rps -> effective throughput fell to ~120 rps
- Error rate: 6% 5xx for the last 12m
- Latency: p99 18.1s, p95 280ms

We've attached a small pcap and our gateway logs. Can you confirm if there are any known issues in the client SDK around header coalescing or streaming reassembly? This is impacting checkouts for a paying merchant — we need an ETA on a fix and any mitigations.

Sara Lim
Engineering Manager — Platform
CheckoutFlow

Attachments: checkoutflow_pcap_snippet.pcap, gateway-errors.log

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@checkoutflow.io>
Cc: monica_patel, rishi_malhotra
Date: 2027-03-25T16:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Live ingestion incident — p99 latency spike and error-rate surge

Sara — thanks for the quick signal. I'm pulling the on-call team now.

Immediate ask: 1) Can you confirm whether you rolled any client-side change to connection pooling or HTTP/2 settings at 15:45 UTC? 2) If you can share the exact request IDs for some 502s I can correlate on our side.

I'll loop in Monica (SDK lead) and Rishi (sales/eng lead for CheckoutFlow) and we'll aim to get a hotfix path within the hour or an explicit mitigation (traffic routing/fallback).

I'll keep you updated every 30 minutes until resolved.

— Markus
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, Sara Lim <sara.lim@checkoutflow.io>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-25T16:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Live ingestion incident — initial triage notes

Quick triage from SDK tests and the pcap you shared:
- Reproduced a steady stream of truncated header frames when client sends many small requests over multiplexed connections.
- Our local harness indicates a header-merge edge-case in the 2.4.x codepath: when consecutive small header blocks arrive, the dechunker occasionally merges header frames without proper boundary markers leading to the server rejecting with 502.
- This manifests under bursty traffic and aggressive connection reuse (exactly your pattern).

Attachments: sdk-headers-log.txt, repro-script.diff

Immediate mitigations we can push:
- Short-term: force connection: close on client side for CheckoutFlow while we patch (loses some keepalive efficiency but restores correctness).
- Mid-term: patch dechunker to strictly validate header boundaries and release 2.4.2 within ~4 hours.

I can produce a small instrumentation build to test on your staging in ~30 minutes. Need a staging toggle or a traffic slice.

— Monica
Staff Software Engineer, SDK Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-25T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Live ingestion incident — bringing leadership up to speed

Looping in Marissa for executive context and to coordinate with CheckoutFlow procurement/CS. This is high-impact for CF (they are a revenue customer on a committed Dedicated plan). Please prioritize the short-term mitigation immediately and prepare a one-pager for the account team.

Marissa — can we schedule a 30m bridge with Sara and the CheckoutFlow exec sponsor at 18:00 UTC? We should offer a credit and an engineering remediation SLA (2.4.2 rollout within 4 hours, stage toggle). Also needs a timeline for a postmortem and root cause analysis.

Rishi
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-25T17:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Live ingestion incident — executive ask and customer comms

Thanks — please do the following ASAP:
- Monica: push the connection: close toggle to CheckoutFlow staging and provide a build link + verification steps.
- Markus: confirm the customers that must be notified and draft a short incident note that we can send from the VP/Sales side. Use clear customer-friendly language and include mitigation steps and ETA.
- Rishi: prepare the commercial remediation (billing credit) proposal — team is fine to use a standard incident credit playbook.

I'll join the 18:00 UTC bridge. Keep communications tight and set expectations: we own this until the patch is live.

— Marissa Cole
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@checkoutflow.io>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: eng@checkoutflow.io, support@checkoutflow.io
Date: 2027-03-26T03:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Live ingestion incident — follow-up and verification

Thanks team — we validated the connection: close toggle on a 5% traffic slice and p99 dropped from 18s to 420ms within 12 minutes. Error rate fell to ~0.3%. Our ops team confirmed no app-level regressions.

Please keep the patch ETA and plan for the 2.4.2 rollout; we'd like a formal postmortem in 48 hours and the root cause write-up to be shareable with our SREs.

Sara Lim
Engineering Manager — Platform
CheckoutFlow

Attachments: verification-screenshot.png
